MOLECULAR CYTOGENETICS REPORT
[redacted name] Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
Department of Haematology-Oncology Genetics

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted]
MRN: [redacted ID]
REFERRING CLINICIAN: Dr [redacted name]
DATE OF COLLECTION: [redacted]
DATE OF REPORT: [redacted]
SPECIMEN TYPE: Lymph node biopsy
SPECIMEN ID: [redacted ID]

CLINICAL DETAILS
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with previous history of follicular lymphoma (FL). Lymph node biopsy submitted for molecular cytogenetic analysis.

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase fluorescence in situ hybridisation (FISH) analysis

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue sections using the following probe sets:
• GeneMark IGH/MYC/CEP8 tri-colour dual fusion probe
• IGH/BCL2 dual colour dual fusion probe
• BCL6 dual colour break apart probe
• MYC dual colour break apart probe

Analysis was performed on areas of tumour identified by correlation with CD20 immunostained slides. A minimum of 100 nuclei were scored for each probe set.

RESULTS - ABNORMAL

IGH/BCL2 t(14;18) rearrangement: POSITIVE
• Fusion signals detected in 78% of nuclei analysed (78/100)
• Pattern consistent with t(14;18)(q32;q21) translocation

MYC (8q24) rearrangement: NEGATIVE
• No evidence of MYC rearrangement
• Normal signal pattern in 96% of nuclei (96/100)

BCL6 (3q27) rearrangement: NEGATIVE
• No evidence of BCL6 rearrangement
• Normal signal pattern in 94% of nuclei (94/100)

INTERPRETATION
This analysis demonstrates the presence of an IGH/BCL2 [t(14;18)] rearrangement. No MYC (8q24) or BCL6 (3q27) rearrangements were detected.

The IGH/BCL2 rearrangement is recognised in both follicular lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. This finding is consistent with transformation from the patient's previous follicular lymphoma.

It should be noted that dual-colour break-apart probes may not detect cryptic insertion events in a small percentage of cases.

This test was performed in a UKAS accredited laboratory (CPA reference: [redacted ID]).

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorised by: Dr [redacted name], Consultant Haematologist
Date: [redacted]
